punchline: The last great auks were killed in 1844; their skins were lost, and DNA later found one in Brussels.
thirty_sec: In 1844 an expedition to Eldey killed the last two great auks seen reliably. The organs went to Copenhagen, but the skins were lost until a 2017 DNA study matched the male's organs to the mounted bird in Brussels.
question: Which object, file or promise changing hands will you be unable to trace in five years?
key_contrast: The birds were kept; their trail was not.
